items.title: Arrival at KIX, transfer to Osaka
items.pace: Evening touchdown — clear immigration and customs, then the JR Haruka straight into Osaka. Nothing else scheduled.
items.tldr: Land at KIX in the evening, ride the Haruka into Osaka, settle in.
items.body:
US passports enter visa-free for tourism (assumed — the intake didn't confirm passport countries). Complete the Visit Japan Web arrival declaration before landing to skip the paper form.

Buy an ICOCA at a KIX ticket machine, then take the JR Haruka limited express to Osaka Station (≈{{fact:haruka-kix-shin-osaka-1800-yen}}, direct). If dinner is wanted on arrival, Kinryu Ramen's Dotonbori Honten runs 24 hours with vending-machine ordering — the low-effort option for a late landing, not a destination meal in its own right.

items.title: Osaka: Castle, Kuromon Ichiba, Dotonbori food crawl
items.pace: A late-morning castle visit, an afternoon browse through Kuromon Ichiba market, then a three-stop Dotonbori dinner crawl after dark.
items.tldr: Osaka Castle by day, then okonomiyaki, kushikatsu and takoyaki after dark.
items.body:
Osaka Castle's keep opens 9:00–18:00 (last entry 17:30), admission {{fact:osaka-castle-admission-1200-yen}} — the surrounding park grounds are free to walk. Late morning avoids both the worst crowds and the midday queue at the ticket counter.

Kuromon Ichiba Market makes a good lunch stop on the walk back toward Namba; go before 11am if the goal is browsing rather than standing in a 30-minute takoyaki line.

Dinner is a three-stop Dotonbori crawl: Mizuno for okonomiyaki (arrive at open, 11:00, or expect a wait — it doesn't take reservations), Kushikatsu Daruma's Dotonbori branch for skewers, and Wanaka for takoyaki to finish. Kani Doraku's giant mechanical crab sign is worth a photo on the way past, but its ¥5,000–10,000/person course pricing and mixed reviews on ingredient quality make it a landmark to look at, not a meal to book. If the canal-front takoyaki line runs long, Kouga-ryu in nearby Amerikamura is the locals' equivalent at the same price point, minus the wait.

items.title: Kyoto: Fushimi Inari at dawn, Higashiyama, Gion & Pontocho
items.pace: Early start for Fushimi Inari before the tour buses arrive, late morning at Kiyomizu-dera and the Higashiyama slope, evening in Gion then a reserved kaiseki dinner in Pontocho.
items.tldr: Torii gates at sunrise, Kiyomizu-dera's wooden stage by late morning, kaiseki in Pontocho at night.
items.body:
Fushimi Inari Taisha is free and open 24 hours. Arrive by 6:30–7am for the empty version of the famous torii tunnel — by 8am the base is crowded. Go only as far as the Yotsutsuji junction (~30–45 min up); past it, the summit loop adds another 1.5–2 hours for a view gain most visitors call marginal.

Kiyomizu-dera opens at 6:00am; closing time shifts by season (~18:00 outside the special night-viewing windows) — confirm the posted hours on arrival. Admission is {{fact:kiyomizu-dera-admission-500-yen}} (sourced to the temple's neighborhood association page, not the temple's own fee page directly — worth reconfirming). Note: this trip does not fall inside a Kiyomizu-dera illumination window — the confirmed 2026 autumn night viewing runs Nov 21–30, after these dates.

In Gion, the public streets (Hanamikoji, Yasaka Shrine) are open as always; stay off the private alleys around Kosode Koji, posted with a ¥10,000 fine since May 2024.

⚠ Toji's own autumn illumination (Oct 31–Dec 13, 18:00–21:00, ¥1,000, no reservation) is the one temple illumination that actually falls inside these dates — Kiyomizu-dera's and Eikando's do not. It isn't built into this already-packed day; see the ledger's traveler question on whether to trade something out for it or save it for a future trip.

Dinner: Houshoan in Pontocho, kaiseki or wagyu-sukiyaki courses ≈¥10,000–13,000/person depending on season. Reserve through its own site — the booking window, cancellation policy and foreign-card acceptance aren't stated on the page, so a follow-up call is worth it. ⚠ Confirm the reservation went through before the day of.

plan_b.body: Nishiki Market's covered arcade (Nishiki-koji St, central Kyoto) is fully weatherproof and reachable by bus/subway from Higashiyama — trade the Fushimi Inari/Kiyomizu-dera walking for a slower morning browsing the market's food stalls instead, then head to Pontocho for the evening as planned. If the rain is light rather than heavy, Nanzenji's Suirokaku aqueduct (same Higashiyama corridor) is a firsthand-corroborated option too — two independent accounts describe it as still worth the walk in a drizzle, just quieter than usual.

items.title: Nara day trip
items.pace: Full day trip to Nara — Todai-ji's Great Buddha Hall, the park's deer, Kasuga Taisha, and a kakinoha-zushi lunch — back to base by evening.
items.tldr: The 15-meter bronze Buddha at Todai-ji, deer in the park, and persimmon-leaf sushi for lunch.
items.body:
From Kyoto, the JR Nara Line rapid runs {{fact:jr-nara-line-kyoto-nara-720-yen}} one-way (~45 min); from Osaka, the Kintetsu Nara Line Limited Express is {{fact:kintetsu-nara-ltd-express-1200-yen}} (~35–40 min) or the non-limited-express Rapid/Express service on the ¥680 base fare, a little slower with no reservation.

Todai-ji's Daibutsuden is open 8:00–17:00 in November, admission {{fact:todaiji-admission-800-yen}}. Nara Park's deer will bite or headbutt if teased or denied food they can see — only feed them the official shika-senbei sold on-site, and show empty palms when you're out. For a quieter deer encounter than the crowded Nandaimon approach, two independent resident blogs point to Asajigahara-en, just north of Ukimido pond.

Kasuga Taisha's main sanctuary is free to visit, 7:00am–5:00pm in November; the inner special-worship area is {{fact:kasuga-taisha-inner-700-yen}}. Lunch: Kakinohazushi Tanaka, a two-minute walk from Kintetsu Nara Station, for kakinoha-zushi (persimmon-leaf-wrapped sushi, a Nara specialty) — no reservation needed.

Both return routes run every 15–30 minutes into the evening; this is not a tight last-train day.
constraints: Kasuga Taisha main sanctuary Nov–Feb hours: 7:00–17:00

items.title: Arashiyama, Nishiki Market, departure prep
items.pace: An early bamboo grove walk, Tenryu-ji's garden, a last pass through Nishiki Market, then wind down toward departure — pace this against the actual outbound flight time, which wasn't given at intake.
items.tldr: Arashiyama's bamboo grove before the crowds, then a slow final morning.
items.body:
The Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is a free public path, best before 8am when it's still empty — by 9:30 it's a shuffle. Pair it with Tenryu-ji next door: garden-only admission {{fact:tenryuji-garden-500-yen}} (+¥300 for building access), 8:30am–5:00pm, but Nov 15–30 the garden opens early at 7:30am — this date qualifies.

Nishiki Market for a final browse: buy from a stall and eat in front of it or inside, rather than walking and eating — the market association's own posted request.

⚠ No outbound flight time was given at intake. Confirm it and work backward from there; this day is written loose on purpose.
